approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Train and activate staff before expecting them to train volunteers. Staff-first sequencing creates training multipliers and reduces the risk that inconsistent volunteer practices damage data quality.

source_refs.title: AI Voice Models & the Hidden Costs of Untrained Staff | Ep 214

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: AI governance should include staff training, data-minimization rules, and a review path before AI-generated content or data summaries influence public communication or pastoral action.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Before staff encounter a changed Rock interface, a short targeted video can prevent avoidable support tickets and reduce surprise. The training should be prepared and distributed as part of the upgrade plan.

source_refs.title: AI Voice Models & the Hidden Costs of Untrained Staff | Ep 214

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Effective dashboards should communicate a clear story, focus attention on decisions, and avoid overloading leaders with more measures than they can act on.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Because AI model capabilities and vendor terms change quickly, churches should document which tools are approved and what data classes may be used with each one.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: When migrating to Rock, teams should ask why a process exists and whether it should be automated or redesigned instead of recreating every legacy step.

source_refs.title: Episode 84: Special Edition with Red Rocks

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Community feedback channels such as Rocket Chat, calls, church visits, and conferences can explain why areas like Connections rise in priority, but agents should treat that as roadmap context rather than proof that a feature is present in a given instance.

source_refs.title: Rock's Future Anchored in Vision | Ep 202

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Before implementing a requested screen, workflow or automation, restate the underlying problem and generate several genuinely distinct approaches. A stakeholder's proposed solution may be valuable requirements evidence without being the best implementation.

source_refs.title: The Vatican on AI and Grandmasters on Ministry | Ep 215

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Wi-Fi presence connects campus network signals to person attendance-style insight, which makes data ownership, vendor behavior, and privacy review part of the implementation guidance.

source_refs.title: Episode 40: v8 and more team updates

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: External BI tools can combine Rock tables, query outputs, spreadsheets, and other data sources into one view, but teams should choose the approach based on resources, expertise, privacy needs, and whether the dashboard needs refresh automation.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The v19 Check-In Manager roster uses real-time updates so attendance state changes can appear without manually refreshing the page. Verify browser connectivity, block version and local check-in configuration when updates lag.

source_refs.title: 3 Underrated Features Churches Are Overlooking | Ep 217

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: This official overview presents Rock as an integrated church-management and digital-ministry platform spanning people, families, giving, check-in, engagement, communications and personalized digital channels. It is a product overview, so agents should route each implementation question to current feature documentation rather than treat the video as a configuration contract.

source_refs.title: A Powerful Open-Source Platform for Your Digital Ministry | Rock RMS

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Self-hosted Rock operators own their patch cadence, and supported dot releases can carry security fixes that should not be treated as optional. Confirm currently supported branches and review current release notes before upgrading.

source_refs.title: The Vatican on AI and Grandmasters on Ministry | Ep 215

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Self-hosted Rock operators own their patch cadence, and supported dot releases can carry security fixes that should not be treated as optional. Confirm currently supported branches and review current release notes before upgrading.

source_refs.title: The Vatican on AI and Grandmasters on Ministry | Ep 215

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: This official Rock AI Summit recording introduces Rock IQ and walks through the full AI Agent framework: staff chat, MCP and voice demonstrations; agent, skill and tool security; Connected Services onboarding; early church and partner prototypes; exploratory MCP UI and knowledge-base ideas; and detailed Lava tool-building guidance. Use the recording for product context, demonstrations and rollout lessons, while using current written documentation, release notes and live configuration as the authority for implementation and availability.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Ministry and program dashboards should avoid standalone numbers when possible; compare measures to goals, historical baselines, or funnels so teams can interpret whether a result needs action.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: MCP UI and a Rock knowledge-base layer for documents, content channels and plugin-provided organizational knowledge are presented as exploratory roadmap work. The summit explicitly says these items are not committed to ship, so agents must not describe them as currently available features without newer evidence.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Core Rock UI and UX work affects the components staff use daily, so developer guidance should consider usability and feedback loops, not just backend behavior.

source_refs.title: Episode 37: Special Edition Garrett Johnson

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: The v19 merge-person interface surfaces last-modified time and actor information so reviewers can compare record recency without separately reconstructing history. Treat recency as one merge signal, not proof that one record is correct.

source_refs.title: New Features & Enhancements Coming to v19

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock data quality work should be prioritized because dirty people, family, address, and duplicate data affects check-in, communication, reporting credibility, and leadership decisions.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Track recurring data defects in a shared backlog, choose a small set of fields or defect types to address first, set measurable cleanup goals, and share wins so ministry teams understand the operational value of clean Rock data.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: This Data Analytics Hub walkthrough gives public-safe guidance for building a layered Rock reporting suite with Power BI or similar tools. It distinguishes executive, campus/ministry, and functional reporting, emphasizes comparison against goals or history, and shows when scheduled refreshes, live queries, Rock security roles, and embedded report pages each fit.

source_refs.title: Media Watch

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock v19 adds workflow actions for sending a Rock Chat channel message or direct message. Verify Rock Chat configuration, recipient resolution, workflow security and delivery behavior before operational use.

source_refs.title: New Features & Enhancements Coming to v19

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: MyWell's prototypes illustrate how partners can add specialized financial skills for tasks such as batch discrepancy diagnosis, processing-fee analysis and recurring-giving health. These examples demonstrate extension patterns and should not be treated as built-in Rock behavior unless the corresponding skill or product is installed and verified.

source_refs.title: AI Summit: The Community's First Look at Rock's AI Agents

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: When BI reports are embedded back into Rock, teams still need to honor external licensing and put report pages behind appropriate Rock security roles.
